To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the disease gene in the FRAX‐MR families is linked to the probe DXS85.
we have identified the disease locus for FRAX‐MR, using RFLPs.
we have shown linkage of FRAX‐MR to Xq27‐qter in three Swedish families.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of DNA markers in the region Xq26‐Xqter.
the development of new diagnostic methods for FRAX‐MR.
the molecular analysis of families with FRAX-MR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FRAX‐MR gene is localized in the region Xq26.1‐Xq27.3 and is closely linked to the probe pXJ.1.
the disease locus is linked to the Xq26 region.
the disease locus is located between the probe Xp22.2 and the distal end (Xqter) of Xq, with a maximum likelihood estimate for the recombination fraction of θ=0.05.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the disease locus for FRAX‐MR is localized to the region Xq26‐Xq27 and that the disease locus and the fragile site are closely linked.
the disease gene is located in the region Xq26‐Xq27, and that the probe pXJ1.2, which is located in the distal end Xq, is the best marker for linkage analysis in FRAX‐MR families.
the disease locus is linked to the Xq27.2‐Xq27.3 region, but that the disease gene may be more distal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of flanking DNA probes is an effective method for the identification of carrier females and prenatal diagnosis in FRAX‐MR.
we can now perform carrier testing in families where the diagnosis of the carrier mother is difficult by the conventional method.
the fragile site in the Xq27.2‐q28 region is not always associated with the disease.
